comparison: Both evaluate claims about Cac-Pr relationships and VGCC levels at different inputs (C3, C16, C17, C23). OpenEval focuses on functional imaging data showing positive correlations and different slopes. Peer review groups these with additional claims (C18-C22) and emphasizes the convincing nature of the analyses across all three reviewers.

Both address claims about Cac levels not explaining Pr differences (C18-C22). OpenEval provides detailed evaluation of confocal imaging showing no significant difference in average Cac but different slopes. Peer review combines these with C3, C16, C17, C23 and affirms findings as convincing through postsynaptic calcium imaging combined with post-hoc Cac-TdTomato imaging.

Perfect match on claims C5, C26-C30 regarding VGCC density differences revealed by STORM imaging. Both evaluations support the findings. OpenEval notes the inference about tighter coupling is reasonable but could be strengthened. Peer review describes these as important advancements showing packing density as a critical determinant of release probability.

Both address Cac:Brp ratio claims (C7, C33-C35). OpenEval supports the data but notes C35 is a hypothesis rather than demonstrated result. Peer review groups these with additional Brp-related claims (C6, C36-C39) and describes findings as interesting though not entirely unexpected, without raising concerns about the hypothetical nature of C35.

Both evaluate Brp correlation claims (C36-C39 overlap). OpenEval focuses on C9, C36-C39 regarding Brp-Cac correlations and differential contributions within versus between inputs. Peer review combines these with C6, C7, C33-C35 in a broader evaluation of Brp findings, affirming them as part of important advancements.

Perfect match on claims C40-C44 regarding reduced Cac levels in brp-/- mutants. Both evaluations support the findings. OpenEval notes C44 is speculation but reasonable. Peer review accepts these as part of convincing analysis on how Brp modulates calcium channel abundance without specifically addressing the speculative nature of C44.

Both address homeostatic potentiation claims (C49-C51). OpenEval supports these as evidence for conserved mechanisms across synaptic subtypes. Peer review combines these with C55-C58 and emphasizes the concerted increase in Cac, Stj, and CaB as providing an interesting new dimension and foundation for future work.

Both evaluate input-specific Brp functions during PHP (C55-C58). OpenEval supports differential effects at two inputs as strong evidence for input-specific functions. Peer review groups these with C49-C51 and highlights the brp-dependent increase in VGCC density as largely responsible for PHP at the Drosophila NMJ.

Both address auxiliary subunit findings, particularly Stj levels (C6, C81-C83, C85). OpenEval supports variable stoichiometry and pool of VGCCs lacking α2δ-3. Peer review combines these with C73-C75, C78, C80 and strongly praises the new tools and finding of reduced Stj at Is active zones as notable and striking.

Both evaluate Stj-Cac correlations (C86-C88). OpenEval supports strong positive correlations at individual AZs but notes direct Stj-Pr data would strengthen conclusions. Peer review emphasizes the concerted increase in Cac, Stj, and CaB after plasticity and notes these lines strongly correlate with Pr at both terminal types.

Both address coordinated increases during homeostatic plasticity (C91-C93). OpenEval supports increased Brp, Cac, and Stj levels with similar percentage increases as evidence for coordinated regulation. Peer review combines these with C95, C124 and explicitly praises the concerted increase as providing an interesting new dimension and foundation for future work.

Both evaluate chronic PHP findings (C95, C124). OpenEval supports increased Stj levels and maintained stoichiometry inference, though notes direct Cac:Stj ratio measurements would strengthen conclusions. Peer review groups these with C91-C93 and praises the demonstration of dynamic structural changes contributing to physiological plasticity.

Perfect match on the integrative model (C98). Both evaluations strongly support this synthesis. OpenEval describes it as well-supported by data on VGCC density, ratios, and correlations, providing a coherent framework. Peer review emphasizes broad implications and important advancements to understanding synaptic diversity and function.

Both address foundational claims about the experimental system (C1-C2, C11-C15). OpenEval supports these based on citations and functional imaging. Peer review combines these with C24-C25 and notes these are established facts confirmed by the authors' data, with no reviewer questioning these foundational claims.

Both address background literature claims (C24-C25). OpenEval supports these as providing important context from prior work. Peer review groups these with C1-C2, C11-C15 as established background facts supported by citations, with no concerns raised.

Both evaluate endogenously tagged subunit expression (C73-C75). OpenEval supports validation of tagged lines and establishment of NMJ presence. Peer review combines these with C78, C80-C83, C85 and strongly praises the new transgenic tools as powerful reagents that will be of wide interest to the field.

Both address auxiliary subunit localization (C78, C80). OpenEval supports findings on localization and similar Ca-β levels at both inputs. Peer review groups these with C73-C75, C81-C83, C85 and emphasizes the novel transgenic animals as expanding molecular tools available for synaptic biology exploration.
